heading: Route rules
body: A route is a path that `RequestRoute` on the controller class and `GetRoute`, `PostRoute` and the other verb annotations on a method declare together. A part in braces, such as `{id}`, is a path variable (a part of the URL that can change). The method reads it with a `FromPath` argument, and its declared type is checked. A fixed path part uses only lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, such as `order-items`. A path variable name uses only lowercase letters, digits and underscores, such as `{order_id}`. The build refuses other characters. A page folder `_id` and a path variable `{id}` name the same route, so a page and a controller can share a path. Two controllers cannot answer the same verb on the same path. This works the same way in every language that Yon runs. Every route also says who may call it: `Public`, `SignedIn` or `Allow(Role)` on the controller class or on the method, and the method wins.
